Scheopner's level gates: Novice -> Intermediate 'Once you are sub-30 or so', Advanced 'Once you are sub-20 or so' (https://www.scheopner.com/cube/). Useful for Rouxtine level brackets alongside the Roux Reader FAQ gates.

csTimer has Roux training-scramble types ('3x3x3 Roux': 2nd Block, CMLL, LSE, LSE <M, U>) and 'Roux S1' / 'Roux S1 + S2' solver tools (src/lang/en-us.js L69, L238-243, L649 @5f8e46cb), but Training Stat. does not identify CMLL cases.

Cubeast's case-order tracker accumulates per-case sums, not means (class Inn in main.843d00e3c1cda244.js). If Rouxtine copies the '8x slowest' bag, it should rank by mean or EMA time to avoid a frequency feedback loop.

cubedex counts a rep as 'successful' unless it is aborted ('again'), so mistaken 'hard' reps still count toward auto-learned, which needs at least 5 reviews and 11 of the last 12 (src/lib/srs.ts @8a8b5b9).

CubeSkills' CFOP reference splits are 'partially based on sub 10 solver data gathered in this speedsolving thread' (threads/a-method-of-cfop-speedcubing-training-that-yields-systematic-progress.39406). The tool only accepts averages strictly between 8 and 60 s.

acubemy's training page (login-gated) says it 'suggests new algorithms to learn based on your skill' (https://acubemy.com/training). Its blog says 'cross training and metronome training' tools are coming (https://acubemy.com/blog/how-to-improve-at-3x3).
